title: Frontend ingest: vectorized UTF-8 scanner and concurrent normalization to cut prefill wall-time
creator: Amelia Tran
description:
Problem: Short prompts and high-QPS routes spend a disproportionate fraction of wall-time in request-side preprocessing (UTF-8 scanning, normalization, whitespace collapsing, and session-prefix dedupe). Current behavior serializes byte scanning and Unicode normalization per-request and re-parses the same session prefixes across concurrent requests, leading to cpu-bound tails and higher p99 latency for low-token requests.

Goal: Reduce per-request preprocessing wall-time for common short-prompt workloads by 40-60% and cut p95/p99 latency contribution from front-end preprocessing by at least 50ms on typical small requests. Keep memory overhead bounded (<5% increase per worker) and preserve identical tokenization outputs (no semantic changes).

Approach (overview):
- Implement a vectorized UTF-8 byte-scan that scans for tokenization-relevant codepoints (whitespace, ascii-range, multibyte starts) using 64-bit lanes where available, falling back to bytewise on constrained targets.
- Move expensive Unicode normalization (NFKC-like steps we do for model alignment) to a lightweight concurrent normalizer service that caches normalized session-prefixes with LRU eviction keyed by session_id + prefix_hash.
- Introduce a short-path fast-check: for purely-ascii inputs (common for code prompts / short queries) skip normalization and heavy parsing and use a stricter but fast tokenizer entrance.
- Add shared prefill warm cache per-session to avoid repeated work when identical prefixes are requested across microbatches. Cache lookup is O(1) with finger-printed keys.
- Expose runtime knobs (env flags) to force strict compat mode (no fast-paths) for A/B testing.

Non-goals: Redesigning the tokenizer algorithm or model-side token handling. This ticket focuses on front-end preprocessing latency and throughput only.
acceptance_criteria: Median preprocessing CPU time for short prompts (<=32 chars) reduced by >=45% compared to current baseline
End-to-end p95 latency contribution from preprocessing reduced by >=50ms on target routes under representative load
No changes to tokenizer outputs for 99.99% of test corpus (full regression suite) and documented, reviewed exceptions for canonical fast-path rules
Memory increase per worker <=5% under representative traffic
Feature gate exists to disable fast-paths and return to strict parsing for compatibility testing
design_decisions: Favor vectorized byte scanning to reduce branch mispredictions and per-byte overhead; accept additional complexity in code to keep hot path minimal
Use a session-scoped LRU cache rather than global dedupe to limit cross-tenant memory amplification and make eviction predictable
Implement fast-path-only for ascii-only requests rather than approximate heuristics to avoid semantic drift
Keep normalization algorithm identical to current production code path; fast-paths will bypass it only when inputs are proven ascii-only or match cached normalized prefix
Expose runtime feature gate instead of compile-time flag to allow gradual rollout and emergency rollback
work_log: 2026-02-25 - Ticket created. Problem observed in customer telemetry: short prompts (<=16 tokens) had preprocessing medians of ~12ms and p99 spikes to 78ms on small instances.

2026-03-01 - Spike implemented in runtime sandbox: vectorized scanner prototype using u64 lanes reduced CPU cycles by ~42% in microbench for ascii-heavy strings. Benchmark script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/bench/tokenizer-vectorized
2026-03-04 - Design review with R&D and infra: agreed to session-scoped cache and feature-gateability. Notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X-TokenizerFastPath-Design

2026-03-07 - Integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1218 - includes vectorized scanning and fast-path branch. Initial CI passed unit tests; integration tests failing on multi-byte edge cases (emoji sequences).
2026-03-09 - Fixed multi-byte start detection and added exhaustive unicode regression tests drawn from our fuzz corpus. Added golden files to tests/tokenizer/goldens

2026-03-11 - Bench on staging (type: small-gpu-worker): median preprocessing time for 32-char prompts dropped from 18.4ms -> 9.1ms (50.5% reduction). Observed p95 contribution down by ~42ms. Memory increase measured at ~3.2% per worker with session cache active.

2026-03-12 - Noted a tail case when concurrent requests probe different prefixes causing cache churn; next action: implement cache admission policy to prefer longer-lived prefixes and add per-session fingerprinting to reduce eviction noise
next_steps: Implement cache admission policy and per-session fingerprint optimizer (Diego)
